---
title: "Candidate ensemble"
---

Place **Candidate ensemble** after **Candidate models**. It uses one weighted
winning configuration from each eligible method, including that configuration's
complete preprocessing pipeline. Five eligible methods produce five available
members. All available members are selected initially.

### Settings

**Member models** selects which method winners participate. **Ensemble style**
offers equal mean or median predictions for regression, and soft or hard voting
for classification. Soft voting averages aligned class probabilities and requires
probabilities from every member. Hard voting uses majority labels, breaking ties
by the stable class order. Members have equal voting weight. The upstream goal
weights select the representatives; they are not prediction weights.

**Preferred metric** changes the chart and the table sort order without refitting models or
changing the upstream representatives. Metric choices follow the outcome task.
Unavailable metrics, such as log loss for hard voting, have no score.

### Evaluation

Members and ensemble are fitted and evaluated on identical resampling splits.
The valid upstream evaluation plan takes precedence. Without a plan, the card
uses the same seeded five-fold defaults as Candidate training, stratified for
classification and reduced for small samples. Grouped, temporal or spatial data
require an explicit plan. Holdout and prediction observations are excluded.

The front chart sorts from best to worst and highlights the ensemble in orange.
Losses appear in their natural units. Hover text and the provisional flip-side
table report fold standard deviation and completed splits for the preferred metric.
The table also shows all feasible task metrics side by side: RMSE, MAE and R²
for regression, and available classification metrics. These are
**post-selection resampling scores**: the member configurations were already
selected using tuning evidence, so this is not independent test performance.

### Ensemble checkbox

With **Ensemble** unticked, the incoming model passes through. Evaluation is
available for comparison. Ticking **Ensemble** exports the ensemble training
definition, its fitted instance for each evaluation split, split memberships and
scores. Each split-fitted ensemble contains member models trained only on that
split's training observations. It is not a single model fitted on all observations.

**Final fitting remains downstream.** A final-fitting card can fit either the
upstream weighted individual winner or this ensemble on the designated final
training observations. The resampling models must not be mistaken for a final
fitted model. Changed members, settings or input invalidate pending evaluation;
export waits for matching results. Upstream training can continue: progress updates
and unrelated trials do not restart evaluation while the selected winners and
other fitting inputs remain unchanged. Fitted evaluation models are session runtime
evidence, not portable bookmark artifacts; restoring the card regenerates them.

Stacking is not offered in this version. It requires an additional inner
resampling design for learning the meta-model without leakage.
